Quickie — iPad layout prototypes

Three throwaway explorations answering: what should the launcher look like on iPad?  ·  PR #239  ·  iPad (A16) simulator, portrait  ·  Aug 8, 2026

The problem

Today: the phone layout, stretched

The app declares iPad support (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2") and runs fine, but the layout is the iPhone UI at full width: the input capsule spans the whole ~10″ screen, the empty state floats in a huge void, and rows read edge-to-edge. Nothing breaks — it just wastes the screen and strains the eye.

Each variant below runs in the real app with mock data, behind the -ipad-prototype A|B|C launch argument, switchable in-app via the floating pill.

The three variants

Variant A

Centered column

Today's layout constrained to a ~620pt centered column. Nothing moves — the content just stops stretching.

  • Keeps bottom-input muscle memory and app identity intact
  • Full-bleed backdrop preserved
  • Lowest risk; smallest diff (frame caps in RootView)
  • Gains nothing from the big screen
  • Side margins are dead space
Effort: small — width caps + padding, no structural change.
Variant B

Split panes

The type→choose→run loop lives in a fixed ~420pt left rail; the freed right side becomes a browsable canvas — large Favorites cards and the Pile at a glance.

  • Only variant that gains capability from the screen
  • Favorites/Pile reachable with zero typing
  • Input stays bottom-anchored, thumb-first
  • Biggest departure from “one input, nothing else”
  • Two surfaces to keep in sync; new interaction rules
  • Needs a landscape story and a Stage Manager story
Effort: large — new navigation model, results routing, state for the right pane.
Variant C

Command palette

Spotlight/Raycast-style floating card over a dimmed backdrop: input on top of the card, results below, macOS reading order.

  • Most iPad-native with a hardware keyboard — genre standard
  • Focused: content and results share one tight surface
  • Scales naturally to landscape and Stage Manager windows
  • Inverts the bottom-input, thumb-first design language
  • Top of screen is a reach in handheld portrait use
  • Reversed result list must flip reading order
Effort: medium — same loop, re-anchored; keyboard-inset logic largely disappears.

Side by side

A — Centered columnB — Split panesC — Command palette

Uses the big screenNoYes — browsing canvasPartially — focus over spread
Hardware-keyboard fitOKOKExcellent
Handheld / touch fitExcellentGoodWeaker (top reach)

Risk to phone layoutNoneNone (size-class gated)None (size-class gated)

Recommendation

Ship A — Centered column now as the low-risk fix: it removes the stretched-phone look for a trivial diff and changes no behavior.

Treat C — Command palette as the destination for a real iPad release: with a Magic Keyboard the top-input palette is how every launcher in the genre behaves, and it retires most of the keyboard-inset complexity. B is worth revisiting only if the iPad app should become a browsing surface rather than a launcher.

Prototype code: App/Quickie/IPadLayoutPrototypeView.swift on branch prototype/ipad-layouts — mock data, unreachable without the launch argument, to be deleted once a direction is folded into RootView. Run: xcrun simctl launch <ipad-udid> com.julesseguin.quickie -ipad-prototype A
